summary: gateio-sdk 99.99.1 exfiltrates host identity and environment variables to attacker endpoint on pip install
details: setup.py defines a pingback() function and invokes it unconditionally at module top-level, so it runs during `pip install` of the sdist. The function collects installer-side host and identity data (whoami, id/privileges, hostname, cwd, platform, timestamp), reads /etc/hosts, and dumps the installer's environment by reading /proc/self/environ on Linux or os.environ elsewhere (truncated to 3000 chars). The collected data is POSTed as JSON to the hardcoded author-controlled endpoint https://pingback.zsdsh.xyz/depconf/gateio-sdk/. Build and CI environments routinely hold cloud credentials, registry tokens, and auth material in environment variables, so this is a bulk credential sweep against the installer. The package is published under the name `gateio-sdk` at the abnormally high version 99.99.1, matching the dependency-confusion resolver-preference shape against a potentially-internal package name, and the package self-describes as a 'dependency confusion PoC' authored by `bytesnull44` — a label that does not change the harm inflicted on anyone who installs it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
